title.zh: 卷五十四 列傳第四: 王世充 竇建德
title.en: Volume 54 Biographies 4: Wang Shicong, Dou Jiande
title.raw: 卷五十四 列傳第四: 王世充 竇建德 Volume 54 Biographies 4: Wang Shicong, Dou Jiande

sentences.zh: 唐儉，字茂約，并州晉陽人，北齊尚書左僕射邕之孫也。

translations.literal: Tang Jian, styled Maoyue, was a native of Jinyang in Bing Province, and was the grandson of Yin, Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat of Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Jian, whose courtesy name was Maoyue, came from Jinyang in Bing Province. He was the grandson of Yin, who had served Northern Qi as Left Vice Director of the Imperial Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父鑑，隋戎州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Jian was Governor of Rong Prefecture under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jian had been governor of Rong Prefecture in Sui times.

sentences.zh: 儉落拓不拘規檢，然事親頗以孝聞。

translations.literal: Jian was unconventional and unbound by rules and regulations, yet in serving his parents he was quite renowned for filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: Jian was free-spirited and heedless of formal propriety, yet he was well known for devotion to his parents.

sentences.zh: 初，鑑與高祖有舊，同領禁衛。

translations.literal: Earlier, Jian's father had old ties with Gaozu and together they led the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: His father had long-standing ties to Gaozu and had served with him commanding the imperial guard.

sentences.zh: 高祖在太原留守，儉與太宗周密，儉從容說太宗以隋室昏亂，天下可圖。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was acting as military governor at Taiyuan, Jian was on intimate terms with Taizong; Jian at leisure urged Taizong that the Sui house was befuddled and chaotic and the empire could be taken.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu held Taiyuan as deputy, Jian grew close to Taizong and, in easy conversation, urged him that the Sui court had lost its way and that the realm might be seized.

sentences.zh: 太宗白高祖，乃召入，密訪時事。

translations.literal: Taizong reported this to Gaozu, who then summoned Jian in and privately asked his view of the times.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong informed Gaozu, who summoned Jian and questioned him privately about current affairs.

sentences.zh: 儉曰：「明公日角龍庭，李氏又在圖牒，天下屬望，非在今朝。

translations.literal: Jian said: "Your Lordship has the horn of the sun and the dragon's forehead; the Li clan is also recorded in prognostications; the empire looks to you—the time is not merely today.
translations.idiomatic: Jian said, "Your Lordship bears the marks of heavenly mandate—the sun-horn and dragon-brow—and the house of Li already appears in prophetic charts. The realm already turns its hopes to you; the moment is not merely today.

sentences.zh: 若開府庫，南嘯豪傑，北招戎狄，東收燕、趙，長驅濟河，據有秦、雍，海內之權，指麾可取。

translations.literal: If you open the storehouses, call the mighty to the south, summon the tribes of the north, take Yan and Zhao in the east, drive swiftly across the Yellow River, hold Qin and Yong, authority within the seas can be taken at a gesture.
translations.idiomatic: Open the treasuries, rally the great families to the south and the frontier peoples to the north, recover Yan and Zhao in the east, sweep across the Yellow River, secure Qin and Yong—and dominion over the empire will be yours to command with a wave of the hand.

sentences.zh: 願弘達節，以順群望，則湯、武之業不遠。」

translations.literal: I pray you will broaden your lofty resolve to accord with the multitude's hopes; then the achievements of Tang and Wu are not far off."
translations.idiomatic: Broaden your great purpose to answer what all expect, and the achievements of the founders of the Shang and Zhou will be within reach."

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「湯、武之事，非所庶幾。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "The deeds of Tang and Wu are not what I dare hope for.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu replied, "The achievements of Tang and Wu are more than I dare aspire to.

sentences.zh: 今天下已亂，言私則圖存，語公則拯溺。

translations.literal: Today the realm is already in turmoil; speaking privately one plots for survival, speaking publicly one would rescue the drowning.
translations.idiomatic: The realm is already in chaos. In private terms one plans to survive; in public terms one would rescue those floundering.

sentences.zh: 卿宜自愛，吾將思之。」

translations.literal: You should take care of yourself; I shall think on this."
translations.idiomatic: Take care of yourself—I will consider what you say."

sentences.zh: 及開大將軍府，授儉記室參軍。

translations.literal: When the Grand General's Office was opened, Jian was appointed Recorder in the staff office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand General's Office was established, Jian was made staff recorder.

sentences.zh: 太宗為渭北道行軍元帥，以儉為司馬。

translations.literal: When Taizong became field marshal for the Weibei circuit, he made Jian his adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took command as Weibei campaign marshal, he appointed Jian chief of staff.

sentences.zh: 平京城，加光祿大夫、相國府記室，封晉昌郡公。

translations.literal: After the pacification of the capital he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and recorder for the Chancellor's Office, and enfeoffed as Duke of Jinchang commandery.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was taken, he was promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and recorder in the Chancellor's Office, and enfeoffed Duke of Jinchang.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，除內史舍人，尋遷中書侍郎，特加授散騎常侍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was made Secretariat Drafter, soon transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat, and specially given the additional title of Formation Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 1 he became Secretariat Drafter, was soon promoted Vice Director of the Secretariat, and was specially granted the additional rank of Formation Attendant.

sentences.zh: 王行本守蒲州城不降，敕工部尚書獨孤懷恩率兵屯於其東，以經略之。

translations.literal: Wang Xingben held Pu Prefecture city and would not surrender; an edict ordered Minister of Works Dugu Huai'en to lead troops encamped east of it to conduct operations.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Xingben held Pu Prefecture and refused to submit. An edict ordered Minister of Works Dugu Huai'en to encamp east of the city and bring it under control.

sentences.zh: 尋又夏縣人呂崇茂以城叛，降於劉武周，高祖遣永安王孝基、工部尚書獨孤懷恩、陝州總管於筠等率兵討之。

translations.literal: Soon after, Lu Chongmao of Xia County rebelled with the city and submitted to Liu Wuzhou; Gaozu sent Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji, Minister of Works Dugu Huai'en, Military Governor of Shan Prefecture Yu Yun and others to lead troops against them.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Lu Chongmao of Xia County mutinied, surrendered his city to Liu Wuzhou, and Gaozu dispatched Prince of Yong'an Xiaoji, Dugu Huai'en, Shan Prefecture military governor Yu Yun, and others against them.

sentences.zh: 時儉使至軍所，屬武周遣兵援崇茂，儉與孝基、筠等並為所獲。

translations.literal: At that time Jian had reached the army camp on a mission; just then Wuzhou sent troops to aid Chongmao, and Jian together with Xiaoji, Yun and the rest were all captured.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had arrived at the camp on official business when Wuzhou sent reinforcements for Chongmao, and Jian, Xiaoji, Yun, and the others were all taken prisoner.

sentences.zh: 初，懷恩屯兵蒲州，與其屬元君實謀反，時君實亦陷於賊中，與儉同被拘執，乃謂儉曰：「古人有言：『當斷不斷，反受其亂。』

translations.literal: Earlier, when Huai'en had encamped at Pu, he and his subordinate Yuan Junshi plotted rebellion; Junshi had also fallen into the rebels' hands and was detained together with Jian, and said to Jian: "The ancients have a saying: 'When one should cut and does not, afterward one suffers disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, while Huai'en had been encamped at Pu, he and his follower Yuan Junshi had plotted revolt. Junshi too had been trapped among the enemy and was held with Jian, and told him, "As the ancients said, 'He who ought to strike and does not will suffer disorder in the end.

sentences.zh: 獨孤尚書近者欲舉兵圖事，遲疑之間，遂至今日，豈不由不斷耶？」

translations.literal: Minister Dugu recently wished to raise troops for a plot, but in the interval of hesitation matters reached today—is this not from not cutting?'"
translations.idiomatic: Minister Dugu wished lately to raise troops for his plot, yet lingered in doubt until things came to this pass—is that not precisely failure to strike when one should?'"

sentences.zh: 俄而懷恩脫身得還，仍令依前屯守，君實又謂儉曰：「獨孤尚書今遂拔難得還，復在蒲州屯守，可謂王者不死。」

translations.literal: Before long Huai'en escaped and returned, and was again ordered to garrison as before; Junshi again said to Jian: "Minister Dugu has now escaped hardship and returned, and again holds Pu in garrison—one may say a true king does not die."
translations.idiomatic: Soon Huai'en slipped away and returned to his old post at Pu. Junshi told Jian again, "Minister Dugu has broken free and resumed command at Pu—a man destined for kingship, it seems, does not perish."

sentences.zh: 儉聞之，懼懷恩為逆，乃密令親信劉世讓以懷恩之謀奏聞。

translations.literal: Hearing this, Jian feared Huai'en would rebel, and secretly had his trusted follower Liu Shirang report Huai'en's plot to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Alarmed, Jian secretly sent his confidant Liu Shirang to report Huai'en's designs to the throne.

sentences.zh: 適遇王行本以蒲州歸降，高祖將入其城，浮舟至中流，世讓謁見，高祖讀奏，大驚曰：「豈非天命也！」

translations.literal: It happened that Wang Xingben surrendered Pu; Gaozu was about to enter the city, and had floated his boat to midstream when Shirang came to audience; Gaozu read the memorial and exclaimed in alarm: "Is this not heaven's command!"
translations.idiomatic: Just then Wang Xingben surrendered Pu. Gaozu was crossing the river by boat to enter the city when Shirang presented himself with the report. Gaozu read it and cried in astonishment, "Can this be anything but fate!"

sentences.zh: 回舟而歸，分捕反者按驗之，懷恩自縊，餘黨伏誅。

translations.literal: He turned the boat and returned, sent parties to seize the rebels and verify them; Huai'en hanged himself and the rest of the faction were executed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the boat turned back, sent men to seize the plotters and investigate, and Huai'en hanged himself while the rest of his party were put to death.

sentences.zh: 俄而太宗擊破武周部將宋金剛，追至太原，武周懼而北走，儉乃封其府庫，收兵甲，以待太宗。

translations.literal: Before long Taizong broke the troops of Wuzhou's general Song Jingang, pursued to Taiyuan, and Wuzhou in fear fled north; Jian then sealed their storehouses, gathered arms and armor, and awaited Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Taizong shattered Liu Wuzhou's general Song Jingang and pursued to Taiyuan; Wuzhou fled north in panic, and Jian sealed the government stores, collected weapons and armor, and awaited Taizong.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉儉身沒虜庭，心存朝闕，復舊官，仍為并州道安撫大使，以便宜從事，並賜獨狐懷恩田宅貲財等。

translations.literal: Gaozu praised Jian for though his body was in the enemy lands his heart remained at court; his former posts were restored, and he was again made Pacification Commissioner for the Bingzhou circuit with discretionary authority, and Dugu Huai'en's fields, houses and goods were also granted.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu praised Jian for keeping his heart loyal though he had been captive among the enemy, restored his former offices, again made him Pacification Commissioner for Bingzhou with discretionary powers, and granted him the fields, residences, and wealth confiscated from Dugu Huai'en.

sentences.zh: 使還，拜禮部尚書，授天策府長史，兼檢校黃門侍郎，封莒國公，與功臣等元勳恕一死，仍除遂州都督，食綿州實封六百戶，圖形凌煙閣。

translations.literal: On his return from mission he was appointed Minister of Rites, given the post of Chief Administrator of the Heavenly Strategies Office and concurrently Acting Vice Director of the Yellow Gate, enfeoffed Duke of Ju, granted with the other founding ministers the privilege of one forgiven death, still made Military Governor of Suizhou with six hundred actual fief households in Mian Prefecture, and his portrait was placed in the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned from duty abroad he became Minister of Rites and Chief Administrator of the Heavenly Strategies Office, while also serving as Acting Vice Director of the Secretariat; he was enfeoffed Duke of Ju, granted with the other founding meritocrats a single pardoned capital offense, appointed military governor of Suizhou with six hundred fief households in Mian Prefecture, and honored with a portrait in the Lingyan Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，使於突厥，說誘之，因以隋蕭後及楊正道以歸。

translations.literal: In the early Zhenguan period he was sent as envoy to the Turks; he persuaded and enticed them, and thereby brought back the Sui empress Xiao and Yang Zhengdao.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he was sent to the Turks, won them by persuasion, and brought back Empress Xiao of Sui and Yang Zhengdao.

sentences.zh: 太宗謂儉曰：「卿觀頡利可圖否？」

translations.literal: Taizong said to Jian: "Do you think Jieli can be taken?"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong asked Jian, "In your view, can Jieli be won over?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「銜國威恩，亦可望獲。」

translations.literal: He replied: "Cherishing the state's majesty and grace, one may also hope to obtain him."
translations.idiomatic: Jian answered, "Given his regard for our empire's majesty and kindness, there is hope of securing him."

sentences.zh: 遂令儉馳傳至虜庭，示之威信。

translations.literal: Thereupon he ordered Jian to hurry by relay post to the barbarians' court and display authority and trust.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong then sent Jian post-haste to the Türk court to display both power and good faith.

sentences.zh: 頡利部落歡然定歸款之計，因而兵眾弛懈。

translations.literal: Jieli's tribes gladly settled on a plan to submit, and in consequence the soldiers grew slack.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli's tribes gladly agreed to surrender, and their forces accordingly grew lax.

sentences.zh: 李靖率輕騎掩襲破之，頡利北走，儉脫身而還。

translations.literal: Li Jing led light cavalry in a surprise attack and broke them; Jieli fled north and Jian escaped and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jing struck with light cavalry and routed them. Jieli fled north, and Jian made his way back alive.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，授民部尚書。

translations.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: A year or so later he was made Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 後從幸洛陽苑射猛獸，群豕突出林中，太宗引弓四發，殪四豕，有雄彘突及馬鐙，儉投馬搏之，太宗拔劍斷豕，顧笑曰：「天策長史，不見上將擊賊耶！

translations.literal: Later, when accompanying the emperor on a visit to the Luoyang park to shoot fierce beasts, a herd of boars burst from the woods; Taizong drew the bow four times and killed four boars; a great boar charged up to the stirrup, Jian leaped from his horse to grapple it, Taizong drew his sword and cut down the boar, turned with a laugh and said: "Chief Administrator of the Heavenly Strategies Office—do you not see your commander striking down the enemy!
translations.idiomatic: Later, while accompanying Taizong on a hunt for fierce game in the Luoyang park, a drove of boars rushed from the woods. Taizong loosed four arrows and killed four; a huge boar charged his stirrup. Jian leapt from his saddle to wrestle it, and Taizong cut it down with his sword, then laughed over his shoulder, "Chief Administrator—do you not see your commander fighting the foe?

sentences.zh: 何懼之甚？」

translations.literal: Why so much fear?"
translations.idiomatic: Why such terror?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「漢祖以馬上得之，不以馬上治之；

translations.literal: He replied: "The Han Founder won the realm on horseback but did not rule it on horseback;
translations.idiomatic: Jian answered, "The founder of Han won the empire from horseback, yet he did not govern it from horseback.

sentences.zh: 陛下以神武定四方，豈復逞雄心於一獸。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty with divine martial prowess has settled the four quarters—how could you again display ambitious spirit over a single beast?"
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty, by divine prowess, has pacified the realm—surely you need not vent heroic passion on one animal."

sentences.zh: 太宗納之，因為罷獵。

translations.literal: Taizong accepted this and on that account stopped the hunt.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong took his counsel and ended the hunt.

sentences.zh: 尋加光祿大夫，又特令其子善識尚豫章公主。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and specially had his son Shanshi marry Princess Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness, and Taizong further had his son Shanshi marry Princess Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 儉在官每盛修肴饌，與親賓縱酒為樂，未嘗以職務留意。

translations.literal: Jian in office constantly prepared lavish feasts, and with kin and guests indulged in wine for pleasure, never paying attention to official duties.
translations.idiomatic: In office Jian constantly staged extravagant banquets and drank freely with relatives and guests, scarcely attending to his duties.

sentences.zh: 又嘗托鹽州刺史張臣合收其私羊，為御史所劾，以舊恩免罪，貶授光祿大夫。

translations.literal: He also once entreated Salt Commissioner Zhang Chenhe to take in his private sheep; the censorate impeached him, but because of old favor he was excused from punishment, demoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He had also asked the Salt Commissioner Zhang Chenhe to hold private sheep for him; impeached by the censorate, he was spared punishment on account of old ties but demoted to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 永徽初，致仕於家，加特進。

translations.literal: In the early Yonghui period he retired at home, with especial promotion to special advance.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yonghui he retired to his home, and was specially promoted to the highest honorary rank.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing he died, aged seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Xianqing 1 at the age of seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 高宗為之舉哀，罷朝三日，贈開府儀同三司、并州都督，賻布帛一千段、粟一千石，賜東園秘器，陪葬昭陵，謚曰襄，官為立碑。

translations.literal: Gaozong mourned him, suspended court for three days, granted the posthumous title of Honored Equal to the Three Excellencies of the Palace Office and Military Governor of Bingzhou, bestowed one thousand bolts of silk and one thousand piculs of grain as funeral gifts, gave the Eastern Garden secret vessels, buried him with honor at Zhaoling, posthumous name Xiang, and officials erected a stele.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong mourned him, closed court for three days, and posthumously appointed him Honored Equal to the Three Excellencies with the title of military governor of Bingzhou. He granted one thousand bolts of silk and one thousand piculs of grain as funeral gifts, bestowed the Eastern Garden secret vessels, had him buried at Zhaoling, gave him the posthumous name Xiang, and had officials erect a stele.

sentences.zh: 儉少子觀，最知名，官至河西令，有文集三卷。

translations.literal: Jian's youngest son Guan was the most renowned, reaching the post of magistrate of Hexi, and had a collected writings in three fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's youngest son Guan was the best known; he rose to magistrate of Hexi and left a collected writings in three fascicles.

sentences.zh: 儉孫從心，神龍中，以子晙娶太平公主女，官至殿中監。

translations.literal: Jian's grandson Congxin, in the Shenlong era, because his son Jun married a daughter of Princess Taiping, reached the post of Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: Jian's grandson Congxin, in the Shenlong era, rose to Director of the Palace Domestic Service after his son Jun married a daughter of Princess Taiping.

sentences.zh: 晙，先天中為太常少卿，坐與太平連謀，伏誅。

translations.literal: Jun, in the Xiantian era was Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, and because of plotting with Taiping was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Jun served as Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices in the Xiantian era and was executed for conspiring with Princess Taiping.

sentences.zh: 長孫順德，文德順聖皇后之族叔也。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Shunde, Zhangsun Shunde, was a clansman uncle of Empress Wende Shunsheng.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Shunde was a clansman uncle of Empress Wende Shunsheng.

sentences.zh: 祖澄，周秦州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Cheng was Governor of Qin Prefecture under Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Cheng had been governor of Qin Prefecture under Northern Zhou.

sentences.zh: 父愷，隋開府。

translations.literal: His father Kai was a Sui Palace Guard commander.
translations.idiomatic: His father Kai had held a Sui palace guard command.

sentences.zh: 順德仕隋右勳衛，避遼東之役，逃匿於太原，深為高祖、太宗所親委。

translations.literal: Shunde served the Sui as a Right Merit Guard, avoided the Liaodong campaign, fled and hid at Taiyuan, and was deeply trusted by Gaozu and Taizong.
translations.idiomatic: Shunde had served the Sui as a Right Merit Guard, evaded the Liaodong campaign, and took refuge at Taiyuan, where Gaozu and Taizong came to rely on him deeply.

sentences.zh: 時群盜並起，郡縣各募兵為備。

translations.literal: At that time bandits rose everywhere, and each commandery and county recruited troops for defense.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rising everywhere, and counties and prefectures were each recruiting troops for defense.

sentences.zh: 太宗外以討賊為名，因令順德與劉弘基等召募，旬月之間，眾至萬餘人，結營於郭下，遂誅王威、高君雅等。

translations.literal: Taizong outwardly took suppressing bandits as his pretext, and therefore ordered Shunde together with Liu Hongji and others to recruit; within a month or so the force reached more than ten thousand, encamped below the city wall, and then executed Wang Wei, Gao Junya and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong used the suppression of bandits as his public pretext and had Shunde, Liu Hongji, and others recruit troops. Within a month they mustered more than ten thousand men, encamped outside the city, and then executed Wang Wei, Gao Junya, and the others.

sentences.zh: 義兵起，拜統軍。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose, he was appointed Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army was raised, he was made commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 從平霍邑，破臨汾，下絳郡，俱有戰功。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Huoyi, breaking Linfen, taking Jiang commandery—all with military achievement.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in pacifying Huoyi, storming Linfen, and capturing Jiang commandery, distinguishing himself in each.

sentences.zh: 尋與劉文靜擊屈突通於潼關，每戰摧鋒。

translations.literal: Soon he with Liu Wenjing attacked Qu Tu Tong at Tong Pass, and in every battle broke the enemy vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined Liu Wenjing in attacking Qu Tu Tong at Tong Pass and in every engagement shattered the enemy van.

sentences.zh: 及通將奔洛陽，順德追及於桃林，執通歸京師，仍略定陝縣。

translations.literal: When Tong was about to flee to Luoyang, Shunde overtook him at Taolin, seized Tong and returned him to the capital, and still broadly pacified Shan County.
translations.idiomatic: When Tong was fleeing toward Luoyang, Shunde overtook him at Taolin, captured him, and brought him back to the capital, then secured Shan County as well.

sentences.zh: 高祖即位，拜左驍衛大將軍，封薛國公。

translations.literal: When Gaozu took the throne, he was appointed General of the Left Martial Tiger Guards and enfeoffed Duke of Xue.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu ascended the throne, Shunde was made General of the Left Martial Tiger Guards and enfeoffed Duke of Xue.

sentences.zh: 武德九年，與秦叔寶等討建成餘黨於玄武門。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Wude he with Qin Shubao and others suppressed the remnant faction of Jiancheng at the Xuanwu Gate.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 9 he joined Qin Shubao and others in suppressing Jiancheng's remaining supporters at the Xuanwu Gate.

sentences.zh: 太宗踐祚，真食千二百戶，特賜以宮女，每宿內省。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended the throne, his actual fief was twelve hundred households; he was specially granted palace women and each night lodged in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Shunde's actual fief was set at twelve hundred households; he was specially granted palace women and often lodged in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 後，順德監奴，受人饋絹事發，太宗謂近臣曰：「順德地居外戚，功即元勳，位高爵厚，足稱富貴。

translations.literal: Later, Shunde's overseer of slaves was found to have accepted silk as a bribe; Taizong said to his close ministers: "Shunde stands as an affinal kinsman, his merit is that of a founding minister, his rank is high and his fief rich—he may well be called wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when it came out that Shunde's slave overseer had accepted silk bribes, Taizong told his close advisers, "Shunde is an imperial in-law and a founding meritocrat; his rank is high and his fief ample—he is already wealthy enough.

sentences.zh: 若能勤覽古今，以自鑑誡，弘益我國家者，朕當與之同有府庫耳。

translations.literal: If he can diligently read past and present and take them as a mirror for self-warning, and broadly benefit our state, I would share the storehouses with him.
translations.idiomatic: If he would study history for his own warning and work to enlarge the state's good, I would share the treasury with him.

sentences.zh: 何乃不遵名節，而貪冒發聞乎！」

translations.literal: Why then does he not observe reputation and integrity, but greed and corruption become known!"
translations.idiomatic: Why does he ignore his good name and let greed become public scandal?"

sentences.zh: 然惜其功，不忍加罪，遂於殿庭賜絹數十匹，以愧其心。

translations.literal: Yet cherishing his merit, he could not bear to punish him, and therefore in the palace hall granted him several tens of bolts of silk to shame his heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Taizong valued his past service and would not punish him. Instead he gave him several dozen bolts of silk in open court, intending to shame him.

sentences.zh: 大理少卿胡演進曰：「順德枉法受財，罪不可恕，奈何又賜之絹？」

translations.literal: Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Hu Yan advanced and said: "Shunde perverted the law and accepted wealth—the crime cannot be forgiven; why again grant him silk?"
translations.idiomatic: Vice Director of the Court of Judicial Review Hu Yan protested, "Shunde perverted the law and took bribes—a crime that cannot be forgiven. Why reward him with silk?"

sentences.zh: 太宗曰：「人生性靈，得絹甚於刑戮；

translations.literal: Taizong said: "Human nature has spirit; receiving silk is heavier than corporal punishment;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong replied, "A man has his pride. For him, receiving silk is worse than punishment;

sentences.zh: 如不知愧，一禽獸耳，殺之何益！」

translations.literal: if he does not know shame, he is but a beast—what use in killing him!"
translations.idiomatic: if he feels no shame, he is no better than a beast, and killing him would serve no purpose."

sentences.zh: 尋坐與李孝常交通除名。

translations.literal: Soon because of association with Li Xiaochang he was struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was struck from the rolls for associating with Li Xiaochang.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，太宗閱功臣圖，見順德之像，閔然憐之，遣宇文士及視其所為，見順德頹然而醉，論者以為達命。

translations.literal: After more than a year Taizong reviewed the portraits of meritocrats, saw Shunde's image, and pitied him with compassion; he sent Yuwen Shiji to observe his conduct, and saw Shunde collapsed in drunkenness—commentators held this showed understanding of fate.
translations.idiomatic: More than a year later Taizong was reviewing the portraits of meritocrats, saw Shunde's likeness, and took pity on him. He sent Yuwen Shiji to observe him and found Shunde sunk in drink; commentators took this as a man who had accepted his lot.

sentences.zh: 召拜澤州刺史，復其爵邑。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Prefect of Ze, and his title and fief were restored.
translations.idiomatic: Shunde was recalled and appointed prefect of Ze, with his title and fief restored.

sentences.zh: 順德素多放縱，不遵法度，及此折節為政，號為明肅。

translations.literal: Shunde had always been much given to license and did not observe the law; at this he restrained himself in governing and was styled clear and stern.
translations.idiomatic: Shunde had long been unrestrained and heedless of law, but now he disciplined himself in office and was praised as a clear and stern administrator.

sentences.zh: 先是，長吏多受百姓饋餉，順德糾擿，一無所容，稱為良牧。

translations.literal: Earlier, senior officials often accepted gifts from the people; Shunde investigated and exposed them, tolerating none, and was called a good governor.
translations.idiomatic: Senior officials had long accepted gifts from the people; Shunde investigated and exposed every case without mercy and was hailed as an excellent prefect.

sentences.zh: 前刺史張長貴、趙士達並佔境內膏腴之田數十頃，順德並劾而追奪，分給貧戶。

translations.literal: The former prefects Zhang Changgui and Zhao Shida had each seized several tens of qing of fertile land within the jurisdiction; Shunde impeached them all and recovered the land, dividing it among poor households.
translations.idiomatic: Former prefects Zhang Changgui and Zhao Shida had each seized dozens of qing of fertile land in the prefecture; Shunde impeached them, recovered the land, and distributed it to poor households.

sentences.zh: 尋又坐事免。

translations.literal: Soon he was again dismissed because of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon dismissed again on account of another offense.

sentences.zh: 發疾，太宗聞而鄙之，謂房玄齡曰：「順德無慷慨之節，多兒女之情，今有此疾，何足問也！」

translations.literal: He fell ill; Taizong heard and despised this, and said to Fang Xuanling: "Shunde lacks a heroic spirit and has much sentiment for wife and children; now he has this illness—what is there worth asking!"
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill, Taizong heard of it with contempt and told Fang Xuanling, "Shunde lacks heroic resolve and is too given to domestic feeling. Now that he is ill, why should we trouble ourselves about him?"

sentences.zh: 未幾而卒，太宗為之罷朝，遣使弔祭，贈荊州都督，謚曰襄。

translations.literal: Before long he died; Taizong suspended court for him, sent envoys to mourn and sacrifice, granted the posthumous title Military Governor of Jingzhou, posthumous name Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after. Taizong closed court in mourning, sent envoys to offer sacrifices, posthumously appointed him military governor of Jingzhou, and gave him the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十三年，追改封為邳國公。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year of Zhenguan his enfeoffment was posthumously changed to Duke of Pi.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 13 his title was posthumously changed to Duke of Pi.

sentences.zh: 永徽五年，重贈開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghui he was again granted Honored Equal to the Three Excellencies of the Palace Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 5 he was again posthumously granted Honored Equal to the Three Excellencies.

sentences.zh: 劉弘基，雍州池陽人也。

translations.literal: Liu Hongji, Liu Hongji, was a native of Chiyang in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Hongji came from Chiyang in Yong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父昇，隋河州刺史。

translations.literal: His father Sheng was Governor of He Prefecture under the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sheng had been governor of He Prefecture in Sui times.

sentences.zh: 弘基少落拓，交通輕俠，不事家產，以父廕為右勳侍。

translations.literal: Hongji in youth was unconventional, associated with light knights-errant, did not attend to family property, and through his father's privilege became a Right Merit Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Hongji was free-spirited, consorted with roaming swordsmen, neglected the family estate, and entered service through his father's privilege as a Right Merit Attendant.

sentences.zh: 大業末，嘗從煬帝征遼東，家貧不能自致，行至汾陰，度已後期當斬，計無所出，遂與同旅屠牛，潛諷吏捕之，繫於縣獄，歲餘，竟以贖論。

translations.literal: At the end of the Daye reign he once followed Emperor Yang on the Liaodong campaign; his family was poor and he could not provide for himself; reaching Fenyin he reckoned he was already late and would be beheaded, and with no plan he together with fellow travelers slaughtered an ox, secretly prompted the clerk to arrest them, and was imprisoned in the county jail; after more than a year he was finally judged by ransom.
translations.idiomatic: Late in the Daye era he followed Emperor Yang on the Liaodong campaign. Too poor to equip himself, he reached Fenyin, realized he was past deadline and would be executed, and in desperation joined fellow travelers in slaughtering an ox, then secretly arranged for officials to arrest them. He spent more than a year in county jail before being released on payment of a fine.

sentences.zh: 事解亡命，盜馬以供衣食，因至太原。

translations.literal: When the matter was resolved he fled as an outlaw, stole horses to supply food and clothing, and thereby reached Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Once released he went into hiding, stole horses to live on, and made his way to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 會高祖鎮太原，遂自結托，又察太宗有非常之度，尤委心焉。

translations.literal: It happened that Gaozu was garrisoning Taiyuan, and he therefore attached himself; he also observed that Taizong had an extraordinary measure, and especially entrusted his heart to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu was posted at Taiyuan, Hongji attached himself to him and saw in Taizong an uncommon caliber, toward whom he gave his fullest trust.

sentences.zh: 由是大蒙親禮，出則連騎，入同臥起。

translations.literal: Thereby he greatly received intimate favor: going out they rode together, coming in they slept and rose together.
translations.idiomatic: He won exceptional favor: they rode together abroad and shared quarters at home.

sentences.zh: 義兵將舉，弘基召募得二千人。

translations.literal: When the righteous army was about to rise, Hongji recruited and obtained two thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous army was about to be raised, Hongji recruited two thousand men.

sentences.zh: 王威、高君雅欲為變，高祖伏弘基及長孫順德於廳事之後，弘基因麾左右執威等。

translations.literal: Wang Wei and Gao Junya wished to make trouble; Gaozu hid Hongji and Zhangsun Shunde behind the hall, and Hongji thereupon commanded those at hand to seize Wei and the rest.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Wei and Gao Junya plotted a coup, Gaozu hid Hongji and Zhangsun Shunde behind the hall, and Hongji ordered his men to seize Wei and the others.

sentences.zh: 又從太宗攻下西河。

translations.literal: He also followed Taizong in attacking and taking Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: He also followed Taizong in capturing Xihe.

sentences.zh: 義軍次賈胡堡，與隋將宋老生戰，破之，進攻霍邑。

translations.literal: The righteous army halted at Jiahu Fort, fought with the Sui general Song Laosheng, broke him, and advanced to attack Huoyi.
translations.idiomatic: The army camped at Jiahu Fort, defeated the Sui general Song Laosheng, and advanced on Huoyi.

sentences.zh: 老生率眾陣於城外，弘基從太宗擊之，老生敗走，棄馬投塹，弘基下斬其首，拜右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: Laosheng led his masses and arrayed outside the city; Hongji followed Taizong in striking him; Laosheng was defeated and fled, abandoned his horse and threw himself into the moat; Hongji dismounted and cut off his head, and was appointed Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: Laosheng drew up his forces outside the city. Hongji followed Taizong in the attack; Laosheng fled, abandoned his horse, and fell into the moat. Hongji dismounted and took his head and was made Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 師至河東，弘基以兵千人先濟河，進下馮翊，為渭北道大使，得便宜從事，以殷開山為副。

translations.literal: When the army reached Hedong, Hongji with a thousand troops first crossed the river, advanced and took Fengyi, was made Ambassador of the Weibei circuit with discretionary authority, and Yin Kaishan was made his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: When the army reached Hedong, Hongji crossed the river first with a thousand men, captured Fengyi, was appointed Weibei circuit ambassador with discretionary authority, and made Yin Kaishan his deputy.

sentences.zh: 西略地扶風，有眾六萬。

translations.literal: He broadly took territory west into Fufeng, and had a force of sixty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He extended operations west into Fufeng until his force numbered sixty thousand.

sentences.zh: 南渡渭水，屯於長安故城，威聲大振，耀軍金光門。

translations.literal: He crossed the Wei River southward, encamped at the old city of Chang'an, his martial renown greatly shook, and displayed his army at the Jinguang Gate.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the Wei to the south, encamped in the old city of Chang'an, and his fame spread far; he paraded his army before the Jinguang Gate.

sentences.zh: 衛文升遣兵來戰，弘基逆擊走之，擒甲士千餘人、馬數百匹。

translations.literal: Wei Wensheng sent troops to fight; Hongji met them in counterattack and drove them off, capturing more than a thousand armored soldiers and several hundred horses.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Wensheng sent troops against him; Hongji counterattacked, routed them, and captured more than a thousand armored soldiers and several hundred horses.

sentences.zh: 時諸軍未至，弘基先至，一戰而捷。

translations.literal: At that time the other armies had not yet arrived; Hongji arrived first and in one battle was victorious.
translations.idiomatic: The other armies had not yet arrived when Hongji reached the field and won the first battle.

sentences.zh: 高祖大悅，賜馬二十匹。

translations.literal: Gaozu was greatly pleased and granted him twenty horses.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was delighted and rewarded him with twenty horses.

sentences.zh: 及破京城，功為第一。

translations.literal: When the capital was broken, his merit ranked first.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell, his merit ranked first.

sentences.zh: 從太宗擊薛舉於扶風，破之，追奔至隴山而返。

translations.literal: He followed Taizong in striking Xue Ju at Fufeng, broke him, pursued the rout to Long Mountain and returned.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizong in defeating Xue Ju at Fufeng, pursued the rout to Long Mountain, and then returned.

sentences.zh: 累拜右領都督，封河間郡公。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly appointed Right Area Commander and enfeoffed as Duke of Hejian Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through repeated appointments to Right Area Commander and was enfeoffed as Duke of Hejian Commandery.

sentences.zh: 又從太宗經略東都，戰於瓔珞門外，破之。

translations.literal: He again followed Taizong in planning operations against the Eastern Capital, fought outside the Yingluo Gate, and broke the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Taizong in operations against the Eastern Capital, fought outside the Yingluo Gate, and defeated the enemy.

sentences.zh: 師旋，弘基為殿。

translations.literal: When the army withdrew, Hongji served as rearguard.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return, Hongji commanded the rearguard.

sentences.zh: 隋將段達、張志陳於三王陵，弘基擊敗之。

translations.literal: The Sui generals Duan Da and Zhang Zhi formed ranks at the Three Kings Mounds; Hongji struck and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui generals Duan Da and Zhang Zhi drew up at the Three Kings Mounds, Hongji routed them.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，拜右驍衛大將軍，以元謀之勳，恕其一死，領行軍左一總管。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude, he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Xiaowei Guard; for his merit in the original plot, one death penalty was forgiven him, and he led the Left First Army General-in-Command.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 1, he was made General-in-Chief of the Right Xiaowei Guard; for his role in the founding conspiracy his death sentence was pardoned, and he took command as Left First Army General-in-Command.

sentences.zh: 又從太宗討薛舉。

translations.literal: He again followed Taizong in campaigning against Xue Ju.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Taizong against Xue Ju.

sentences.zh: 時太宗以疾頓於高墌城，弘基、劉文靜等與舉接戰於淺水原，王師不利，八總管咸敗；

translations.literal: At that time Taizong, ill, halted at Gaogai City; Hongji, Liu Wenjing, and others joined battle with Ju at Qianshui Plain; the imperial army fared ill, and all eight commanders-in-chief were defeated;
translations.idiomatic: Taizong, stricken with illness, halted at Gaogai City. Hongji, Liu Wenjing, and others fought Ju at Qianshui Plain, but the imperial forces fared badly and all eight commanders-in-chief were defeated;

sentences.zh: 唯弘基一軍盡力苦鬥，矢盡，為舉所獲。

translations.literal: Only Hongji's single army exerted all effort in bitter fighting; when arrows were exhausted, he was captured by Ju.
translations.idiomatic: Only Hongji's corps fought on to the last; when their arrows ran out, he was taken by Ju.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘉其臨難不屈，賜其家粟帛甚厚。

translations.literal: Gaozu praised his refusal to yield in dire straits and bestowed grain and silk on his household in great measure.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu honored his steadfastness under fire and richly rewarded his family with grain and silk.

sentences.zh: 仁杲平，得歸，復其官爵。

translations.literal: When Rengao was pacified, he was able to return and his offices and titles were restored.
translations.idiomatic: After Rengao was pacified, he returned and his rank and titles were restored.

sentences.zh: 會宋金剛陷太原，遣弘基屯晉州。

translations.literal: When Song Jingang took Taiyuan, Hongji was sent to garrison Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: When Song Jingang captured Taiyuan, Hongji was dispatched to hold Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 裴寂為宋金剛所敗，人情崩駭，莫有固志。

translations.literal: Pei Ji was defeated by Song Jingang; public sentiment collapsed in terror, and none had firm resolve.
translations.idiomatic: After Pei Ji was routed by Song Jingang, morale collapsed and no one held firm.

sentences.zh: 金剛以兵造城下，弘基不能守，復陷於賊。

translations.literal: Jingang brought troops to the city walls; Hongji could not hold and again fell into the rebels' hands.
translations.idiomatic: Jingang marched on the city; Hongji could not hold it and was captured by the rebels again.

sentences.zh: 俄得逃歸，高祖慰諭之，授左一總管。

translations.literal: Soon he escaped and returned; Gaozu comforted and instructed him and appointed him Left First Army General-in-Command.
translations.idiomatic: He soon escaped and returned; Gaozu received him warmly and appointed him Left First Army General-in-Command.

sentences.zh: 從太宗屯於柏壁，率兵二千自隰州趨西河，斷賊歸路。

translations.literal: Following Taizong he encamped at Baiyu, led two thousand troops from Xi Prefecture toward Xihe, and cut off the rebels' route of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizong to Baiyu, led two thousand men from Xi Prefecture toward Xihe, and cut the rebels' line of retreat.

sentences.zh: 時賊鋒甚勁，弘基堅壁，不能進。

translations.literal: At that time the rebel spearhead was very fierce; Hongji fortified his walls and could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: The rebel advance was too strong; Hongji held his fortifications and could not push forward.

sentences.zh: 及金剛遁，弘基率騎邀之，至於介休，與太宗會，追擊大破之。

translations.literal: When Jingang fled, Hongji led cavalry to intercept him, reaching Jiexiu, joined Taizong, pursued, and utterly defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingang fled, Hongji led cavalry in pursuit as far as Jiexiu, joined Taizong there, and together they routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 累封任國公。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly enfeoffed until made Duke of Renguo.
translations.idiomatic: He was repeatedly promoted in rank until enfeoffed as Duke of Renguo.

sentences.zh: 尋從擊劉黑闥於洺州，師旋，授秉鉞將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he followed in striking Liu Heita at Mozhou; when the army returned, he was appointed Bearer of the Battle-Axe General.
translations.idiomatic: He soon joined the campaign against Liu Heita at Mozhou and, on the army's return, was made Bearer of the Battle-Axe General.

sentences.zh: 會突厥入寇，弘基率步騎一萬，自豳州北界東拒子午嶺，西接臨涇，修營障塞，副淮安王神通，備胡寇於北鄙。

translations.literal: When the Turks raided, Hongji led ten thousand infantry and cavalry from Bin Prefecture's northern border east to block Ziwu Ridge and west to connect with Linjing, building camps, barriers, and fortifications; as deputy to Prince Huai'an Li Shentong, he prepared against barbarian raids on the northern frontier.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks invaded, Hongji led ten thousand infantry and cavalry from Bin's northern frontier, east to Ziwu Ridge and west to Linjing, building fortifications. Serving under Prince Huai'an Li Shentong, he defended the northern border against barbarian raids.

sentences.zh: 九年，以佐命功，真食九百戶。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, for his merit in founding the dynasty, his permanent fief was set at nine hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he received a permanent fief of nine hundred households for his founding service.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，顧待益隆。

translations.literal: When Taizong acceded, his regard and favor grew ever greater.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong took the throne, Hongji received even greater favor.

sentences.zh: 李孝常、長孫安業之謀逆也，坐與交遊除名。

translations.literal: When Li Xiaochang and Zhangsun Anye plotted rebellion, he was struck from the rolls for associating with them.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Xiaochang and Zhangsun Anye plotted treason, he was stripped of rank for his association with them.

sentences.zh: 歲餘，起為易州刺史，復其封爵，征拜衛尉卿。

translations.literal: After more than a year, he was raised up as prefect of Yi Prefecture, his enfeoffment was restored, and he was summoned and appointed Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a year he was restored as prefect of Yi Prefecture, regained his title, and was summoned to serve as Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia.

sentences.zh: 九年，改封夔國公，世襲朗州刺史，例停不行。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Kuiguo with hereditary appointment as prefect of Lang Prefecture, but by precedent this hereditary office was not carried out.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he was made Duke of Kuiguo with hereditary rights to the Langzhou prefecture, though the hereditary appointment was not exercised per precedent.

sentences.zh: 後以年老乞骸骨，授輔國大將軍，朝朔望，祿賜同於職事。

translations.literal: Later, citing old age he requested retirement; he was granted General Who Assists the State, attended court on the first and fifteenth of the month, and salary and gifts were the same as for active office.
translations.idiomatic: Later he asked to retire on account of age and was made General Who Assists the State, attending court on the first and fifteenth while receiving the same salary and perquisites as if still in office.

sentences.zh: 太宗征遼東，以弘基為前軍大總管。

translations.literal: When Taizong campaigned against Liaodong, Hongji was made Grand General-in-Command of the vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: On Taizong's Liaodong campaign, Hongji served as Grand General-in-Command of the vanguard.

sentences.zh: 從擊高延壽於駐蹕山，力戰有功，太宗屢加勞勉。

translations.literal: He followed in striking Gao Yanshou at Zhudibushan, fought hard with merit, and Taizong repeatedly added praise and encouragement.
translations.idiomatic: He fought Gao Yanshou at Zhudibushan with distinction, and Taizong repeatedly praised and encouraged him.

sentences.zh: 永徽元年加實封通前一千一百戶。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yonghui his permanent fief was increased to eleven hundred households including previous grants.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 1 his permanent fief was raised to a total of eleven hundred households.

sentences.zh: 其年卒，年六十九。

translations.literal: That year he died, aged sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died that same year at sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 高宗為之舉哀，廢朝三日，贈開府儀同三司、并州都督，陪葬昭陵，仍為立碑，謚曰襄。

translations.literal: Gaozong held mourning for him, suspended court for three days, posthumously granted him Grand Master for the Palace with Golden Bangle and Area Commander of Bing Prefecture, buried him alongside Zhaoling, had a stele erected for him, and gave him the posthumous name Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong mourned him with a three-day suspension of court, posthumously made him Grand Master for the Palace with Golden Bangle and Area Commander of Bing Prefecture, had him buried at Zhaoling with a commemorative stele, and granted the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 弘基遺令給諸子奴婢各十五人、良田五頃，謂所親曰：「若賢，固不藉多財；

translations.literal: Hongji's final instructions granted each of his sons fifteen bondsmen and bondswomen and five qing of fine land; he told those close to him: "If they are worthy, they surely need not rely on great wealth;
translations.idiomatic: In his final instructions Hongji left each son fifteen servants and five qing of good land, telling those close to him: "If they are worthy, they will not need great wealth;

sentences.zh: 不賢，守此可以免飢凍。」

translations.literal: If they are unworthy, holding to this can spare them hunger and cold."
translations.idiomatic: if they are not, this will at least keep hunger and cold at bay."

sentences.zh: 余財悉以散施。

translations.literal: All remaining property he entirely distributed in charity.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered that all remaining wealth be given away in charity.

sentences.zh: 子仁實襲，官至左典戎衛郎將。

translations.literal: His son Renshi inherited the title and rose to Captain of the Left Guard of the Hall of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His son Renshi inherited the title and rose to captain in the Left Guard of the Hall of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 從子仁景，神龍初，官至司農卿。

translations.literal: His nephew Renjing, in the early Shenlong era, rose to Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Renjing rose to Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries in the early Shenlong era.

sentences.zh: 殷嶠殷嶠，字開山，雍州鄠縣人，陳司農卿不害孫也。

translations.literal: Yin Qiao, styled Kaishan, was a native of Hu County in Yong Prefecture and a grandson of Bu Hai, Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Qiao, styled Kaishan, came from Hu County in Yong Prefecture and was a grandson of Bu Hai, Chen's Minister of the Court of the Imperial Granaries.

sentences.zh: 其先本居陳郡，陳亡，徙關中。

translations.literal: His ancestors originally dwelt in Chen Commandery; when Chen perished they moved to the Guanzhong region.
translations.idiomatic: His family originally lived in Chen Commandery and moved to Guanzhong after Chen fell.

sentences.zh: 父僧首，隋秘書丞，有名於世。

translations.literal: His father Sengshou was Deputy Director of the Secretariat under Sui and had fame in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His father Sengshou served as Deputy Director of the Secretariat under the Sui and was widely known.

sentences.zh: 嶠少以學行見稱，尤工尺牘。

translations.literal: Qiao from youth was praised for learning and conduct and was especially skilled at letters.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao was admired from youth for scholarship and character and was especially gifted at correspondence.

sentences.zh: 仕隋太谷長，有治名。

translations.literal: He served Sui as magistrate of Taigu and had a reputation for good governance.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Taigu under the Sui he earned a reputation for effective governance.

sentences.zh: 義兵起，召補大將軍府掾，參預謀略，授心腹之寄，累以軍功拜光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the righteous army rose he was summoned and appointed as an aide in the Generalissimo's office, took part in planning, was entrusted as a confidant, and through repeated military achievement was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising began he was summoned to the Generalissimo's staff, took part in planning, was treated as a trusted confidant, and rose to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness through repeated military achievement.

sentences.zh: 從隱太子攻克西河。

translations.literal: He followed the Hidden Crown Prince in attacking and taking Xihe.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Hidden Crown Prince in capturing Xihe.

sentences.zh: 太宗為渭北道元帥，引為長史。

translations.literal: When Taizong was Grand Marshal of the Weibei circuit, he was brought in as Chief Clerk.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong became Grand Marshal of the Weibei circuit, Qiao was appointed his chief clerk.

sentences.zh: 時關中群盜往往聚結，眾無適從，令嶠招慰之，所至皆下。

translations.literal: At that time bandits in Guanzhong often gathered in groups and the masses had no leader to follow; Qiao was ordered to summon and reassure them, and wherever he went all submitted.
translations.idiomatic: With bandits rampant in Guanzhong and the people without a clear leader, Qiao was sent to win them over, and wherever he went they submitted.

sentences.zh: 又與統軍劉弘基率兵六萬屯長安故城，隋將衛孝節自金光門出戰，嶠與弘基擊破之。

translations.literal: He also with Army Commander Liu Hongji led sixty thousand troops to encamp in the old city of Chang'an; the Sui general Wei Xiaojie came out to fight from the Jinguang Gate, and Qiao with Hongji struck and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He and Army Commander Liu Hongji then led sixty thousand men to camp in the old city of Chang'an. When the Sui general Wei Xiaojie sallied from the Jinguang Gate, Qiao and Hongji routed him.

sentences.zh: 京城平，賜爵陳郡公，遷丞相府掾。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified he was granted the title Duke of Chen Commandery and was transferred to an aide in the Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: After the capital was pacified he was made Duke of Chen Commandery and transferred to the Chancellor's staff.

sentences.zh: 尋授吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Vice Minister of the Board of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 從擊薛舉，為元帥府司馬。

translations.literal: He followed in striking Xue Ju and served as Army Supervisor of the Grand Marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Xue Ju as army supervisor on the grand marshal's staff.

sentences.zh: 時太宗有疾，委軍於劉文靜，誡之曰：「賊眾遠來，利在急戰，難與爭鋒。

translations.literal: At that time Taizong was ill and entrusted the army to Liu Wenjing, admonishing him: "The rebel masses have come from afar; their advantage lies in swift battle—it is hard to contend with their spearhead.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was ill and entrusted the army to Liu Wenjing, warning him: "The enemy has marched far; they want a quick fight, and it is hard to meet their spearhead head-on.

sentences.zh: 且宜持久，待糧盡，然後可圖。」

translations.literal: For now one should endure, wait until grain is exhausted, and only then can they be taken."
translations.idiomatic: Hold on and wait until their supplies run out—only then can we move against them."

sentences.zh: 嶠退謂文靜曰：「王體不安，慮公不濟，故發此言。

translations.literal: Qiao withdrew and said to Wenjing: "The Prince's body is unwell; fearing you would not succeed, he spoke thus.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao withdrew and told Wenjing: "The Prince is ill and fears you might fail—that is why he said that.

sentences.zh: 宜因機破賊，何乃以勍敵遺王也！」

translations.literal: One ought to seize the moment and break the rebels—why leave so fierce an enemy for the Prince!"
translations.idiomatic: We should strike now and break the enemy—why leave such a formidable foe for the Prince to face!"

sentences.zh: 久之，言於文靜曰：「王不豫，恐賊輕我，請耀武以威之。」

translations.literal: After some time he said to Wenjing: "The Prince is unwell; I fear the rebels will look down on us—please display martial might to awe them."
translations.idiomatic: Later he told Wenjing: "With the Prince ill, the enemy may despise us. Let us display our strength to intimidate them."

sentences.zh: 遂陳兵於折墌，為舉所乘，軍乃大敗。

translations.literal: Thereupon they arrayed troops at Zhedi, were exploited by Ju, and the army was utterly defeated.
translations.idiomatic: They duly drew up at Zhedi, Ju seized the opportunity, and the army suffered a crushing defeat.

sentences.zh: 嶠坐減死除名。

translations.literal: Qiao was punished by commutation of death and struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao's death sentence was commuted and he was stripped of rank.

sentences.zh: 後從平薛仁杲，復其爵位。

translations.literal: Later he followed in pacifying Xue Rengao and his titles were restored.
translations.idiomatic: He later helped pacify Xue Rengao and regained his titles.

sentences.zh: 武德二年，兼陝東道大行台兵部尚書，遷吏部尚書。

translations.literal: In the second year of Wude he concurrently served as Minister of War of the Grand Commissioner of the Shandong circuit and was transferred to Minister of the Board of Civil Office.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 2 he concurrently served as Minister of War on the Shandong Grand Commissioner staff and was then transferred to Minister of the Board of Civil Office.

sentences.zh: 從太宗討平王世充，以功進爵鄖國公。

translations.literal: He followed Taizong in campaigning to pacify Wang Shichong and for merit was advanced to Duke of Yun State.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Taizong in defeating Wang Shichong and was raised to Duke of Yun for his service.

sentences.zh: 復從征劉黑闥，道病卒。

translations.literal: He again followed in campaigning against Liu Heita and died of illness on the road.
translations.idiomatic: He again joined the campaign against Liu Heita but died of illness en route.

sentences.zh: 太宗親臨喪，哭之甚慟，贈陝東道大行台右僕射，謚曰節。

translations.literal: Taizong personally attended the mourning, wept with great grief, posthumously granted him Right Vice Commissioner of the Shandong Grand Commissioner, and gave the posthumous name Jie.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong came in person to mourn him and wept bitterly, posthumously making him Right Vice Commissioner of the Shandong Grand Commissioner and granting the posthumous name Jie.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十四年，詔與贈司空、淮安王神通，贈司空、河間王孝恭，贈民部尚書劉政會，俱以佐命功配饗高祖廟庭。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year of Zhenguan an edict ordered that he, together with the posthumously granted Sikong Prince Huai'an Li Shentong, the posthumously granted Sikong Prince of Hejian Li Xiaogong, and the posthumously granted Minister of the Board of Revenue Liu Zhenghui, all for founding merit share sacrifices in Gaozu's temple hall.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 14 an edict ordered that he, alongside the posthumously honored Sikong Prince Huai'an Li Shentong, Sikong Prince of Hejian Li Xiaogong, and Minister of the Board of Revenue Liu Zhenghui, all share sacrifices in Gaozu's temple for their founding service.

sentences.zh: 十七年，又與長孫無忌、唐儉、長孫順德、劉弘基、劉政會、柴紹等十七人，俱圖其形於凌煙閣。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was also, together with Zhangsun Wuji, Tang Jian, Zhangsun Shunde, Liu Hongji, Liu Zhenghui, Chai Shao, and others—seventeen in all—portrayed in likeness at the Lingyan Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year his likeness was painted at the Lingyan Pavilion along with those of Zhangsun Wuji, Tang Jian, Zhangsun Shunde, Liu Hongji, Liu Zhenghui, Chai Shao, and fourteen others—seventeen in all.

sentences.zh: 永徽五年，追贈司空。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghui he was posthumously granted Sikong.
translations.idiomatic: In Yonghui 5 he was posthumously honored as Sikong.

sentences.zh: 嶠從祖弟聞禮，有文學，武德中，為太子中舍人，修梁史，未就而卒。

translations.literal: Qiao's younger cousin of the same clan Wenli had literary talent; in the Wude era he served as Attendant in the Crown Prince's household, compiled the History of Liang, and died before completing it.
translations.idiomatic: Qiao's younger clansman Wenli was a man of letters who served as crown prince attendant in the Wude era, began compiling the History of Liang, and died before finishing it.

sentences.zh: 聞禮子仲容，亦知名，則天深愛其才。

translations.literal: Wenli's son Zhongrong was also well known, and Empress Wu deeply prized his talent.
translations.idiomatic: Wenli's son Zhongrong was also celebrated, and Empress Wu greatly admired his talent.

sentences.zh: 官至申州刺史。

translations.literal: He rose to prefect of Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to prefect of Shen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 劉政會，滑州胙城人也。

translations.literal: Liu Zhenghui was a native of Zuocheng in Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Zhenghui came from Zuocheng in Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖環雋，北齊中書侍郎。

translations.literal: His grandfather Huanjun was Vice Director of the Secretariat of Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Huanjun served as Vice Director of the Secretariat under Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 政會，隋大業中為太原鷹揚府司馬。

translations.literal: Zhenghui, in the Daye era of Sui, served as Adjutant of the Hawk-raising Garrison of Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Sui in the Daye era, Zhenghui served as adjutant of the Taiyuan Hawk-raising Garrison.

sentences.zh: 高祖為太原留守，政會率兵隸於麾下。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was garrison commander of Taiyuan, Zhenghui led troops and placed himself under his command.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu served as garrison commander of Taiyuan, Zhenghui placed his troops under Gaozu's command.

sentences.zh: 太宗與劉文靜謀起義兵，副留守王威、高君雅獨懷猜貳。

translations.literal: Taizong and Liu Wenjing plotted to raise the righteous army; the deputy garrison commanders Wang Wei and Gao Junya alone harbored doubts and divided loyalties.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong and Liu Wenjing plotted the uprising while the deputy commanders Wang Wei and Gao Junya alone remained suspicious and disloyal.

sentences.zh: 後數日，將大會於晉祠，威與君雅謀危高祖。

translations.literal: Several days later, when a great assembly was to be held at the Jin Shrine, Wei and Junya plotted to endanger Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: Days later, as a great assembly was planned at the Jin Shrine, Wei and Junya plotted against Gaozu's life.

sentences.zh: 有人以白，太宗既知迫急，欲先事誅之，因遣政會為急變之書，詣留守告威等二人謀反。

translations.literal: Someone reported this; Taizong, knowing the urgency, wished to strike first and kill them, and so dispatched Zhenghui with an urgent memorial to the garrison headquarters reporting that Wei and the other two men plotted rebellion.
translations.idiomatic: Word reached Taizong of the plot; knowing time was short, he moved to strike first and sent Zhenghui with an urgent report to headquarters accusing Wei and the others of treason.

sentences.zh: 是日，高祖與威、君雅同坐視事，文靜引政會入，至庭中，雲有密狀，知人欲反。

translations.literal: That day Gaozu sat with Wei and Junya jointly handling affairs; Wenjing led Zhenghui in; reaching the courtyard he said there was a secret memorial and that he knew men who wished to rebel.
translations.idiomatic: That day Gaozu was conducting business with Wei and Junya when Wenjing brought Zhenghui before the court and announced a secret report of an impending rebellion.

sentences.zh: 高祖指威等令視之，政會不肯，曰：「所告是副留守事，唯唐公得省之耳。」

translations.literal: Gaozu pointed at Wei and the others and ordered them to look; Zhenghui refused, saying: "What is reported concerns the deputy garrison commanders; only the Duke of Tang may examine it."
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu told Wei and the others to view the report, but Zhenghui refused: "This concerns the deputy commanders—it may be shown only to the Duke of Tang."

sentences.zh: 君雅攘袂大呼曰：「此是反人，欲殺我也！」

translations.literal: Junya flung back his sleeves and shouted: "These are rebels who want to kill me!"
translations.idiomatic: Junya threw up his sleeves and cried out: "These are traitors who mean to kill me!"

sentences.zh: 時太宗已列兵馬佈於街巷，文靜因令左右引威等囚於別室。

translations.literal: At that time Taizong had already arrayed troops in the streets and lanes; Wenjing thereupon ordered attendants to lead Wei and the others away and imprison them in a separate room.
translations.idiomatic: By then Taizong had already deployed troops in the streets; Wenjing had Wei and the others seized and confined in another room.

sentences.zh: 既拘威等，竟得舉兵，政會之功也。

translations.literal: Once Wei and the others were detained, they were finally able to raise the army—this was Zhenghui's achievement.
translations.idiomatic: With Wei and the others secured, the uprising could proceed—an achievement owed to Zhenghui.

sentences.zh: 大將軍府建，引為戶曹參軍。

translations.literal: When the Generalissimo's headquarters was established he was brought in as Registrar of the Household Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: When the Generalissimo's headquarters was established, he was appointed registrar of the Household Bureau.

sentences.zh: 從平長安，除丞相府掾。

translations.literal: He followed in pacifying Chang'an and was appointed an aide in the Chancellor's office.
translations.idiomatic: After Chang'an was pacified he joined the Chancellor's staff.

sentences.zh: 武德初，授衛尉少卿，留守太原。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he was appointed Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia and remained to garrison Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Wude he was made Vice Minister of the Court of Imperial Regalia and left to hold Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 政會內輯軍士，外和戎狄，遠近莫不悅服。

translations.literal: Zhenghui within coordinated the soldiers and without harmonized with the barbarians; near and far none failed to submit in satisfaction.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenghui kept the garrison in order at home and maintained good relations with neighboring tribes; people near and far submitted willingly.

sentences.zh: 尋而劉武周進逼并州，晉陽豪右薛深等以城應賊，政會為賊所擒，於賊中密表論武周形勢。

translations.literal: Soon Liu Wuzhou pressed close upon Bing Prefecture; the powerful families of Jinyang, Xue Shen and others, opened the city to the rebels; Zhenghui was captured by the rebels and from among them sent secret memorials assessing Wuzhou's situation.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wuzhou pressed Bingzhou, local magnates in Jinyang including Xue Shen opened the gates to him. Zhenghui was captured but sent secret reports on Wuzhou's situation from inside enemy lines.

sentences.zh: 賊平，復其官爵。

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified his offices and titles were restored.
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were defeated his rank and titles were restored.

sentences.zh: 歷刑部尚書、光祿卿，封邢國公。

translations.literal: He served successively as Minister of Justice and Minister of the Court of Imperial Banquets and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xing State.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as Minister of Justice and Minister of the Court of Imperial Banquets and was enfeoffed as Duke of Xing.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，累轉洪州都督，賜實封三百戶。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhenguan he was repeatedly transferred until made Area Commander of Hong Prefecture and granted a permanent fief of three hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he rose to Area Commander of Hong Prefecture and received a permanent fief of three hundred households.

sentences.zh: 九年卒，太宗手敕曰：「舉義之日，實有殊功，所葬並宜優厚。」

translations.literal: In the ninth year he died; Taizong wrote in his own hand: "On the day the righteous army was raised he truly had exceptional merit; his burial should all be treated with generous honor."
translations.idiomatic: He died in the ninth year. Taizong wrote in his own hand: "On the day we raised the army he rendered exceptional service; his burial should be treated with the greatest honor."

sentences.zh: 贈民部尚書，謚曰襄。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Minister of the Board of Revenue and given the posthumous name Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously made Minister of the Board of Revenue and granted the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 後與殷開山同配饗高祖廟庭。

translations.literal: Later he shared sacrifices in Gaozu's temple hall together with Yin Kaishan.
translations.idiomatic: He was later granted shared sacrifice in Gaozu's temple alongside Yin Kaishan.

sentences.zh: 子玄意襲爵，改封渝國公，尚南平公主，授駙馬都尉。

translations.literal: His son Xuanyi inherited the title, was re-enfeoffed as Duke of Yu State, married Princess Nanping, and was appointed Commandant of the Emperor's Son-in-Law's Household.
translations.idiomatic: His son Xuanyi inherited the title, was made Duke of Yu, married Princess Nanping, and was appointed commandant of the emperor's sons-in-law.

sentences.zh: 高宗時為汝州刺史。

translations.literal: Under Gaozong he served as prefect of Ru Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Under Gaozong he served as prefect of Ru Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 次子奇，長壽中為天官侍郎，為酷吏所陷也。

translations.literal: The second son Qi, in the Changshou era served as Vice Director of the Bureau of Celestial Offices and was trapped by harsh officials.
translations.idiomatic: The second son Qi served as Vice Director of the Bureau of Celestial Offices in the Changshou era and was destroyed by the harsh officials.

sentences.zh: 柴紹，字嗣昌，晉州臨汾人也。

translations.literal: Chai Shao, styled Sichang, was a native of Linfen in Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chai Shao, styled Sichang, came from Linfen in Jin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖烈，周驃騎大將軍，歷遂、梁二州刺史，封冠軍縣公。

translations.literal: His grandfather Lie was General of Fast Cavalry under Zhou, served successively as prefect of Sui and Liang prefectures, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Guanjun County.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Lie was a Zhou general of fast cavalry who served as prefect of Sui and Liang prefectures and was enfeoffed as Duke of Guanjun County.

sentences.zh: 父慎，隋太子右內率，封鉅鹿郡公。

translations.literal: His father Shen was Right Inner Leader of the Crown Prince under Sui and was enfeoffed as Duke of Julu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shen served as Right Inner Leader of the Crown Prince under the Sui and was enfeoffed as Duke of Julu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 紹幼趫捷有勇力，任俠聞於關中。

translations.literal: Shao from youth was quick and agile with courage and strength; his chivalrous reputation was known throughout Guanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Shao was swift, strong, and brave, and his reputation as a man of chivalry spread throughout Guanzhong.

sentences.zh: 少補隋元德太子千牛備身。

translations.literal: In youth he was appointed as Thousand-Ox Guard Attendant to the Yuande Crown Prince of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: In his youth he served as a guard attendant to the Sui Yuande Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 高祖微時，妻之以女，即平陽公主也。

translations.literal: When Gaozu was still obscure he gave him his daughter in marriage—that is, the Princess of Pingyang.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozu was still obscure he gave Shao his daughter in marriage—the Princess of Pingyang.

sentences.zh: 義旗建，紹自京間路趣太原。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner was raised, Shao by a path through the capital region hastened to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising began, Shao made his way through the capital region to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 時建成、元吉自河東往，會於道，建成謀於紹曰：「追書甚急，恐已起事。

translations.literal: At that time Jiancheng and Yuanji were coming from Hedong; they met on the road, and Jiancheng plotted with Shao, saying: "The pursuit orders are very urgent; I fear the uprising has already begun.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng and Yuanji were traveling from Hedong when they met Shao on the road. Jiancheng confided to him, "The summons to return is urgent—I fear Father has already risen in arms.

sentences.zh: 隋郡縣連城千有餘裡，中間偷路，勢必不全，今欲且投小賊，權以自濟。」

translations.literal: The Sui prefectures and counties are linked in walled towns for more than a thousand li; if we take shortcuts in between, we will surely not arrive intact. For now I wish to throw in our lot with some petty bandits as a temporary expedient to save ourselves."
translations.idiomatic: Sui prefectures and counties are walled and linked for more than a thousand li. If we cut across between them, we cannot hope to get through whole. I mean to throw in with some petty bandits for the moment and save ourselves as best we can."

sentences.zh: 紹曰：「不可。

translations.literal: Shao said: "That will not do.
translations.idiomatic: Shao replied, "No.

sentences.zh: 追既急，宜速去，雖稍辛苦，終當獲全。

translations.literal: The pursuit is already urgent—you should go quickly. Though the journey will be somewhat arduous, in the end you should still escape intact.
translations.idiomatic: The pursuit is already pressing. You should flee at once. The road will be hard, but in the end you can still come through safely.

sentences.zh: 若投小賊，知君唐公之子，執以為功，徒然死耳。」

translations.literal: If you throw in with petty bandits, once they learn you are sons of the Duke of Tang they will seize you for their own merit—and you will die for nothing."
translations.idiomatic: If you join some petty bandits and they learn you are the Duke of Tang's sons, they will seize you for their own credit—and you will have died for nothing."

sentences.zh: 建成從之，遂共走太原。

translations.literal: Jiancheng followed his advice, and together they fled to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Jiancheng took his advice, and together they fled to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 入雀鼠谷，知已起義，於是相賀，以紹之計為得。

translations.literal: Entering Sparrow-and-Rat Pass, they learned the uprising had already begun; they congratulated one another and judged Shao's plan the right one.
translations.idiomatic: When they entered Sparrow-and-Rat Pass and learned the uprising had already begun, they congratulated one another and agreed that Shao's counsel had been right.

sentences.zh: 授右領軍大都督府長史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Chief Clerk of the Right Army Aide Staff of the Grand Army Commander.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed chief clerk of the Right Army Aide Staff of the Grand Army Commander.

sentences.zh: 大軍發晉陽，兼領馬軍總管。

translations.literal: When the main army set out from Jinyang, he concurrently served as Army General-in-Command of the Cavalry Corps.
translations.idiomatic: When the main army marched from Jinyang, he also served as general-in-command of the cavalry corps.

sentences.zh: 將至霍邑，紹先至城下，察宋老生形勢，白曰：「老生有匹夫之勇，我師若到，必來出戰，戰則成擒矣。」

translations.literal: As they were about to reach Huoyi, Shao went ahead to below the city wall, observed Song Laosheng's disposition, and reported: "Laosheng has the courage of a common brawler. If our army arrives, he is sure to come out and fight—and once he fights, he can be captured."
translations.idiomatic: As the army approached Huoyi, Shao rode ahead to scout Song Laosheng below the walls and reported, "Laosheng has nothing but a common brawler's courage. When our army arrives he is sure to come out—and once he does, we can take him."

sentences.zh: 及義師至，老生果出，紹力戰有功。

translations.literal: When the righteous army arrived, Laosheng did indeed come out; Shao fought fiercely and distinguished himself.
translations.idiomatic: When the army arrived, Laosheng did come out as predicted. Shao fought hard and earned distinction.

sentences.zh: 下臨汾，平絳郡，並先登陷陣，授右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: At the fall of Linfen and pacification of Jiang Commandery, he was first to scale the walls and breach the ranks in both cases, and was appointed Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: At the capture of Linfen and pacification of Jiang Commandery he was first over the walls and first into the breach on both occasions, and was made Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 隋將桑顯和來擊，孫華率精銳渡河以援之，紹引軍直掩其背，與史大奈合勢擊之，顯和大敗，因與諸將進下京城。

translations.literal: The Sui general Sang Xianhe came to attack; Sun Hua led elite troops across the river to reinforce him. Shao led his army straight to strike their rear, and joining forces with Shi Dana struck them; Xianhe was routed, and he then advanced with the other generals to take the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When the Sui general Sang Xianhe attacked, Sun Hua led elite troops across the river to reinforce him. Shao swung his army straight at their rear and, joining Shi Dana, crushed them. Xianhe was routed, and Shao then advanced with the other generals to take the capital.

sentences.zh: 武德元年，累遷左翊衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Wude he was promoted in succession to General-in-Chief of the Left Wing Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Wude 1 he rose to General-in-Chief of the Left Wing Guard.

sentences.zh: 尋從太宗平薛舉，破宋金剛，攻平王世充於洛陽，擒竇建德於武牢，封霍國公，賜實封千二百戶，轉右驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he followed Taizong in pacifying Xue Ju, defeating Song Jingang, attacking and pacifying Wang Shichong at Luoyang, and capturing Dou Jiande at Wulao; he was enfeoffed Duke of Huo, granted a substantive fief of twelve hundred households, and transferred to General-in-Chief of the Right Xiaowei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He soon followed Taizong in pacifying Xue Ju, defeating Song Jingang, reducing Wang Shichong at Luoyang, and capturing Dou Jiande at Wulao. He was enfeoffed Duke of Huo with a substantive fief of twelve hundred households and made General-in-Chief of the Right Xiaowei Guard.

sentences.zh: 吐谷渾與党項俱來寇邊，命紹討之。

translations.literal: Tuyuhun and the Tangut together raided the border; Shao was ordered to campaign against them.
translations.idiomatic: When Tuyuhun and the Tangut raided the frontier together, Shao was ordered to campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 虜據高臨下，射紹軍中，矢下如雨。

translations.literal: The barbarians held the high ground and looked down, shooting into Shao's army until arrows fell like rain.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy held the heights and rained arrows down on Shao's army until they fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 紹乃遣人彈胡琵琶，二女子對舞，虜異之，駐弓矢而相與聚觀。

translations.literal: Shao then had someone play the hu pipa and two women dance facing each other; the barbarians, astonished, lowered their bows and arrows and gathered to watch together.
translations.idiomatic: Shao then had a hu pipa played and two women dance facing each other. The barbarians, astonished, lowered their bows and gathered to watch.

sentences.zh: 紹見虜陣不整，密使精騎自後擊之，虜大潰，斬首五百餘級。

translations.literal: When Shao saw the barbarian formation in disorder, he secretly sent elite cavalry to strike from the rear; the barbarians routed in great confusion, and more than five hundred heads were cut off.
translations.idiomatic: Seeing the enemy ranks fall out of order, Shao secretly sent elite cavalry to strike from the rear. The barbarians broke in rout, and more than five hundred heads were taken.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，拜右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 1 he was appointed General-in-Chief of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 二年，擊梁師都於夏州，平之。

translations.literal: In the second year he attacked Liang Shidu at Xia Prefecture and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he attacked Liang Shidu at Xia Prefecture and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 轉左衛大將軍，出為華州刺史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and went out as prefect of Hua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Guard and sent out as prefect of Hua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 七年，加鎮軍大將軍，行右驍衛大將軍，改封譙國公。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was advanced to Grand General of Garrison Troops, acted as General-in-Chief of the Right Xiaowei Guard, and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was advanced to Grand General of Garrison Troops, acted as General-in-Chief of the Right Xiaowei Guard, and was re-enfeoffed Duke of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 十二年，寢疾，太宗親自臨問。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he fell ill in bed; Taizong personally came to inquire after him.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he took to his bed with illness, and Taizong came in person to inquire after him.

sentences.zh: 尋卒，贈荊州都督，謚曰襄。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he died; he was posthumously appointed Area Commander of Jing Prefecture, with the posthumous name Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon after and was posthumously made Area Commander of Jing Prefecture, with the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 平陽公主，高祖第三女也，太穆皇后所生。

translations.literal: The Princess of Pingyang was Gaozu's third daughter, born of Empress Taimu.
translations.idiomatic: The Princess of Pingyang. She was Gaozu's third daughter, born of Empress Taimu.

sentences.zh: 義兵將起，公主與紹並在長安，遣使密召之。

translations.literal: As the righteous army was about to rise, the princess and Shao were both in Chang'an; she sent messengers to summon him in secret.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising was about to begin, the princess and Shao were both in Chang'an. She sent messengers to summon him in secret.

sentences.zh: 紹謂公主曰：「尊公將掃清多難，紹欲迎接義旗；

translations.literal: Shao said to the princess: "Your honored father is about to sweep away many troubles; Shao wishes to go meet the righteous banner;
translations.idiomatic: Shao told the princess, "Your father is about to sweep away the realm's troubles, and I mean to go join the righteous banner.

sentences.zh: 同去則不可，獨行恐罹後患，為計若何？」

translations.literal: We cannot go together, yet if I go alone I fear you will suffer afterward—what plan should we make?"
