translations.idiomatic: We cannot go together, yet if I go alone I fear you will be left in danger afterward. What are we to do?"

sentences.zh: 公主曰：「君宜速去。

translations.literal: The princess said: "You should go quickly.
translations.idiomatic: The princess said, "Go at once.

sentences.zh: 我一婦人，臨時易可藏隱，當別自為計矣。」

translations.literal: I am but a woman and can easily be hidden for the moment; I shall make my own separate plan."
translations.idiomatic: I am only a woman and can hide easily for the moment. I shall make my own plan."

sentences.zh: 紹即間行赴太原。

translations.literal: Shao then made his way secretly to Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Shao then made his way secretly to Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 公主乃歸鄠縣莊所，遂散家資，招引山中亡命，得數百人，起兵以應高祖。

translations.literal: The princess then returned to the family estate in Hu County, distributed the household wealth, recruited fugitives from the mountains, gathered several hundred men, and raised troops in response to Gaozu.
translations.idiomatic: The princess returned to the family estate in Hu County, spent the household fortune, gathered fugitives from the hills until she had several hundred men, and raised troops in answer to Gaozu.

sentences.zh: 時有胡賊何潘仁聚眾於司竹園，自稱總管，未有所屬。

translations.literal: At that time the barbarian bandit He Panren had gathered a force at Sizhu Garden, styled himself Commander-in-Chief, and had not yet attached himself to any cause.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the bandit He Panren had gathered followers at Sizhu Garden, styled himself commander-in-chief, and had not yet pledged himself to any cause.

sentences.zh: 公主遣家僮馬三寶說以利害，潘仁攻鄠縣，陷之。

translations.literal: The princess sent her household retainer Ma Sanbao to persuade him with arguments of advantage and harm; Panren attacked Hu County and took it.
translations.idiomatic: The princess sent her retainer Ma Sanbao to win him over with arguments of gain and loss. Panren then attacked Hu County and took it.

sentences.zh: 三寶又說群盜李仲文、向善志、丘師利等，各率眾數千人來會。

translations.literal: Sanbao also persuaded the bandit chiefs Li Zhongwen, Xiang Shanzhi, Qiu Shili, and others; each led several thousand followers to join her.
translations.idiomatic: Sanbao also won over the bandit chiefs Li Zhongwen, Xiang Shanzhi, Qiu Shili, and others, each of whom brought several thousand followers to join her.

sentences.zh: 時京師留守頻遣軍討公主，三寶、潘仁屢挫其鋒。

translations.literal: At that time the capital garrison repeatedly sent armies against the princess; Sanbao and Panren repeatedly blunted their spearheads.
translations.idiomatic: The capital garrison repeatedly sent troops against the princess, and Sanbao and Panren repeatedly turned them back.

sentences.zh: 公主掠地至盩厔、武功、始平，皆下之。

translations.literal: The princess seized territory as far as Zhouzhi, Wugong, and Shiping, and took them all.
translations.idiomatic: The princess extended her hold as far as Zhouzhi, Wugong, and Shiping, taking them all.

sentences.zh: 每申明法令，禁兵士，無得侵掠，故遠近奔赴者甚眾，得兵七萬人。

translations.literal: She repeatedly proclaimed the laws and forbade the soldiers from plunder, so many rallied from near and far, and she raised an army of seventy thousand.
translations.idiomatic: She repeatedly proclaimed the laws and forbade her soldiers to plunder, so men rallied from far and near until her force reached seventy thousand.

sentences.zh: 公主令間使以聞，高祖大悅。

translations.literal: The princess had a secret messenger report this; Gaozu was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: The princess sent a secret messenger with the news, and Gaozu was greatly pleased.

sentences.zh: 及義軍渡河，遣紹將數百騎趨華陰，傍南山以迎公主。

translations.literal: When the righteous army crossed the river, he sent Shao with several hundred cavalry to hasten to Huayin along the southern mountains to meet the princess.
translations.idiomatic: When the army crossed the river, Gaozu sent Shao with several hundred cavalry along the southern mountains to Huayin to meet the princess.

sentences.zh: 時公主引精兵萬餘與太宗軍會於渭北，與紹各置幕府，俱圍京城，營中號曰「娘子軍」。

translations.literal: At that time the princess led more than ten thousand elite troops and joined Taizong's army north of the Wei; she and Shao each established a headquarters staff, and together besieged the capital; the camp was called the "Lady General's Army."
translations.idiomatic: The princess then led more than ten thousand elite troops to join Taizong north of the Wei. She and Shao each established a staff, and together they besieged the capital. Their camp was called the "Lady General's Army."

sentences.zh: 京城平，封為平陽公主，以獨有軍功，每賞賜異於他主。

translations.literal: When the capital was pacified, she was enfeoffed Princess of Pingyang; because she alone had military merit, her rewards each time differed from those of other princesses.
translations.idiomatic: When the capital fell she was enfeoffed Princess of Pingyang. Because she alone had earned military merit, her rewards always exceeded those of other princesses.

sentences.zh: 六年，薨。

translations.literal: In the sixth year she died.
translations.idiomatic: She died in the sixth year.

sentences.zh: 及將葬，詔加前後部羽葆鼓吹、大輅、麾幢、班劍四十人、虎賁甲卒。

translations.literal: When she was about to be buried, an edict added front and rear plumed-canopy escorts with martial music, the great imperial carriage, command banners, forty sword-bearers in formal array, and tiger-guard armored soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: When she was to be buried, an edict granted front and rear plumed-canopy escorts with martial music, the great imperial carriage, command banners, forty sword-bearers in formal array, and tiger-guard armored soldiers.

sentences.zh: 太常奏議，以禮，婦人無鼓吹。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized that by ritual, women are not granted martial music escorts.
translations.idiomatic: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices memorialized that by ritual women were not granted martial music escorts.

sentences.zh: 高祖曰：「鼓吹，軍樂也。

translations.literal: Gaozu said: "Martial music escorts are military music.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu said, "Martial music escorts are military music.

sentences.zh: 往者公主於司竹舉兵以應義旗，親執金鼓，有克定之勳。

translations.literal: In the past the princess raised troops at Sizhu in response to the righteous banner, personally wielded drum and gong, and had merit in conquering and pacifying.
translations.idiomatic: In the past the princess raised troops at Sizhu in answer to the righteous banner, herself wielded drum and gong, and had merit in pacifying the realm.

sentences.zh: 周之文母，列於十亂；

translations.literal: The mother of King Wen of Zhou was listed among the ten ministers who brought order from chaos;
translations.idiomatic: The mother of King Wen of Zhou was numbered among the ten ministers who brought order from chaos;

sentences.zh: 公主功參佐命，非常婦人之所匹也。

translations.literal: the princess's merit shared in founding the mandate—she is not to be matched by ordinary women.
translations.idiomatic: the princess's merit shared in founding the mandate. She is not to be matched by ordinary women.

sentences.zh: 何得無鼓吹！」

translations.literal: How can she be denied martial music escorts!"
translations.idiomatic: How can she be denied martial music escorts!"

sentences.zh: 遂特加之，以旌殊績；

translations.literal: It was specially granted to honor her extraordinary achievement;
translations.idiomatic: The honor was specially granted to mark her extraordinary achievement;

sentences.zh: 仍令所司按謚法「明德有功曰昭」，謚公主為昭。

translations.literal: and the responsible offices were ordered, according to the posthumous-name code "Illustrious virtue with achievement is called Zhao," to give the princess the posthumous name Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: and the responsible offices were ordered, under the posthumous-name code that "illustrious virtue with achievement is called Zhao," to give the princess the posthumous name Zhao.

sentences.zh: 子哲威，歷右屯營將軍，襲爵譙國公。

translations.literal: His son Zhewei served successively as General of the Right Stationing Camp and inherited the title Duke of Qiao.
translations.idiomatic: His son Zhewei served as General of the Right Stationing Camp and inherited the title Duke of Qiao.

sentences.zh: 坐弟令武謀反，徙嶺南。

translations.literal: For his younger brother Lingwu's plot of rebellion, he was banished to Lingnan.
translations.idiomatic: Because his younger brother Lingwu plotted rebellion, he was banished to Lingnan.

sentences.zh: 起為交州都督，卒官。

translations.literal: He was recalled to serve as Area Commander of Jiao Prefecture and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later recalled to serve as Area Commander of Jiao Prefecture and died in office.

sentences.zh: 令武尚巴陵公主，累除太僕少卿、衛州刺史，封襄陽郡公。

translations.literal: Lingwu married the Princess of Baling; he was repeatedly appointed Vice Minister of the Stud and prefect of Wei Prefecture, and was enfeoffed Duke of Xiangyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Lingwu married the Princess of Baling, rose through appointments as Vice Minister of the Stud and prefect of Wei Prefecture, and was enfeoffed Duke of Xiangyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 永徽中，坐與公主及房遺愛謀反，遣使收之。

translations.literal: In the Yonghui era, for involvement in rebellion with the princess and Fang Yi'ai, envoys were sent to seize him.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yonghui era he was implicated in rebellion with the princess and Fang Yi'ai, and envoys were sent to seize him.

sentences.zh: 行至華陰，自殺，仍戮其屍。

translations.literal: When he reached Huayin he killed himself, and his corpse was still mutilated in punishment.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Huayin he killed himself, but his corpse was still mutilated in punishment.

sentences.zh: 公主賜死。

translations.literal: The princess was granted death.
translations.idiomatic: The princess was ordered to take her own life.

sentences.zh: 馬三寶，初以平京城功，拜太子監門率。

translations.literal: Ma Sanbao was first, for merit in pacifying the capital, appointed Crown Prince Gate Supervisor.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sanbao. For merit in pacifying the capital he was first appointed Crown Prince Gate Supervisor.

sentences.zh: 別擊叛胡劉拔真於北山，破之。

translations.literal: Separately he attacked the rebel barbarian Liu Bazhen at North Mountain and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: He separately attacked the rebel Liu Bazhen at North Mountain and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 又從平薛仁杲，遷左驍衛將軍。

translations.literal: He again followed in pacifying Xue Renguo and was transferred to General of the Left Xiaowei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He again took part in pacifying Xue Renguo and was transferred to General of the Left Xiaowei Guard.

sentences.zh: 復從柴紹擊吐谷渾於岷州，先鋒陷陣，斬其名王，前後虜男女數千口，累封新興縣公。

translations.literal: Again he followed Chai Shao in attacking Tuyuhun at Min Prefecture; as vanguard he breached the ranks, beheaded their famous king, and in all captured several thousand men and women; he was repeatedly enfeoffed Duke of Xinxing County.
translations.idiomatic: Again he followed Chai Shao against Tuyuhun at Min Prefecture. As vanguard he broke the enemy ranks, beheaded their famous king, and captured several thousand men and women in all. He was repeatedly enfeoffed Duke of Xinxing County.

sentences.zh: 嘗從幸司竹，高祖顧謂三寶曰：「是汝建英雄之處，衛青大不惡！」

translations.literal: Once when he accompanied the imperial progress to Sizhu, Gaozu turned and said to Sanbao: "This is where you built your heroic career—Wei Qing was not so bad!"
translations.idiomatic: Once, accompanying the imperial progress to Sizhu, Gaozu turned to Sanbao and said, "This is where you made your name—a career worthy of Wei Qing!"

sentences.zh: 累除左驍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to General-in-Chief of the Left Xiaowei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in succession to General-in-Chief of the Left Xiaowei Guard.

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the third year of Zhenguan.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Zhenguan 3.

sentences.zh: 太宗為之廢朝，謚曰忠。

translations.literal: Taizong canceled court for him and gave him the posthumous name Zhong.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong suspended court for him and granted the posthumous name Zhong.

sentences.zh: 武士鸊，并州文水人也。

translations.literal: Wu Shiyi was a native of Wenshui in Bing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shiyi came from Wenshui in Bing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 家富於財，頗好交結。

translations.literal: His household was rich in wealth and he was quite fond of forming connections.
translations.idiomatic: His family was wealthy and he was fond of cultivating connections.

sentences.zh: 高祖初行軍於汾、晉，休止其家；

translations.literal: When Gaozu first marched through Fen and Jin, he rested at Shiyi's home;
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu first marched through Fen and Jin, he lodged at Shiyi's home;

sentences.zh: 因蒙顧接，及為太原留守，引為行軍司鎧。

translations.literal: there he received Gaozu's attention and favor, and when Gaozu became Taiyuan garrison commander, Shiyi was brought in as Army Equipment Officer in the campaign staff.
translations.idiomatic: where Gaozu favored him. When Gaozu became Taiyuan garrison commander, Shiyi was brought in as army equipment officer on the campaign staff.

sentences.zh: 時盜賊蜂起，士鸊嘗陰勸高祖舉兵，自進兵書及符瑞，高祖謂曰：「幸勿多言。

translations.literal: At that time bandits swarmed everywhere; Shiyi once secretly urged Gaozu to raise troops and himself presented military texts and portents. Gaozu said to him: "Please say no more.
translations.idiomatic: Bandits were rising everywhere. Shiyi once secretly urged Gaozu to raise troops and himself presented military texts and portents. Gaozu told him, "Say no more.

sentences.zh: 兵書禁物，尚能將來，深識雅意，當同富貴耳。」

translations.literal: Military texts are forbidden objects—yet you were still able to bring them. I deeply appreciate your refined intent; we shall share fortune together."
translations.idiomatic: Military texts are forbidden, yet you brought them anyway. I understand your intent well—we shall share fortune together."

sentences.zh: 及義兵將起，高祖募人，遣劉弘基、長孫順德等分統之。

translations.literal: When the righteous army was about to rise, Gaozu recruited men and sent Liu Hongji, Zhangsun Shunde, and others to command them separately.
translations.idiomatic: When the uprising was about to begin, Gaozu recruited men and sent Liu Hongji, Zhangsun Shunde, and others to command them separately.

sentences.zh: 王威、高君雅陰謂士鸊曰：「弘基等皆背征三衛，所犯當死，安得領兵？

translations.literal: Wang Wei and Gao Junya secretly said to Shiyi: "Hongji and the others all evaded the third campaign levy—they have committed offenses warranting death; how can they lead troops?
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei and Gao Junya secretly told Shiyi, "Hongji and the others all evaded the third campaign levy. Their offense warrants death—how can they be allowed to lead troops?

sentences.zh: 吾欲禁身推覈。」

translations.literal: We wish to confine them and investigate."
translations.idiomatic: We mean to detain them and investigate."

sentences.zh: 士鸊曰：「此並唐公之客也，若爾，便大紛紜。」

translations.literal: Shiyi said: "These are all the Duke of Tang's retainers; if you do that, there will be great turmoil."
translations.idiomatic: Shiyi said, "These are all the Duke of Tang's men. If you do that, there will be chaos."

sentences.zh: 威等由是疑而不發。

translations.literal: Wei and the others therefore harbored doubts and did not act.
translations.idiomatic: Wei and the others therefore hesitated and did not act.

sentences.zh: 留守司兵田德平又欲勸威等鞫問募人之狀，士鸊謂德平曰：「討捕之兵，總隸唐公。

translations.literal: The garrison Army Affairs Officer Tian Deping again wished to urge Wei and the others to interrogate those recruited; Shiyi said to Deping: "The troops for pursuit and capture all fall under the Duke of Tang.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison army affairs officer Tian Deping again wanted to urge Wei and the others to interrogate the recruits. Shiyi told Deping, "The pursuit troops all answer to the Duke of Tang.

sentences.zh: 王威、高君雅等，並寄坐耳，彼何能為！」

translations.literal: Wang Wei, Gao Junya, and the like are merely nominal presences—what can they do!"
translations.idiomatic: Wang Wei, Gao Junya, and the like are only nominal presences—what can they do!"

sentences.zh: 德平遂止。

translations.literal: Deping then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Deping then dropped the matter.

sentences.zh: 義旗起，以士鸊為大將軍府鎧曹。

translations.literal: When the righteous banner rose, Shiyi was made Equipment Section head of the Grand General's Office.
translations.idiomatic: When the righteous banner rose, Shiyi was made head of the equipment section in the Grand General's Office.

sentences.zh: 從平京城功，拜光祿大夫，封太原郡公。

translations.literal: For merit in pacifying the capital he was appointed Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed Duke of Taiyuan Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: For merit in pacifying the capital he was made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness and enfeoffed Duke of Taiyuan Commandery.

sentences.zh: 初為義師將起，士鸊不預知，及平京師，乃自說云：「嘗夢高祖入西京，升為天子。」

translations.literal: At first, when the righteous army was about to rise, Shiyi had not been forewarned; after the capital was pacified he then claimed for himself: "I once dreamed that Gaozu entered the Western Capital and ascended as Son of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the uprising was about to begin, Shiyi had not been forewarned. After the capital was pacified he claimed, "I once dreamed that Gaozu entered the Western Capital and ascended as Son of Heaven."

sentences.zh: 高祖哂之曰：「汝王威之黨也。

translations.literal: Gaozu smiled and said: "You were Wang Wei's party.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu smiled and said, "You were Wang Wei's man.

sentences.zh: 以汝能諫止弘基等，微心可錄，故加酬效；

translations.literal: Because you could advise against moving against Hongji and the others, a slight loyal intent is worth recording, so reward was added;
translations.idiomatic: Because you could dissuade them from moving against Hongji and the others, a trace of loyal intent is worth noting, so I rewarded you;

sentences.zh: 今見事成，乃說迂誕而取媚也？」

translations.literal: now that you see success, you spin fanciful tales to flatter me?"
translations.idiomatic: now that you see success, you spin fanciful tales to flatter me?"

sentences.zh: 武德中，累遷工部尚書，進封應國公，又歷利州、荊州都督。

translations.literal: In the Wude era he was promoted in succession to Minister of Works, advanced to Duke of Ying, and also served as Area Commander of Li and Jing prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: In the Wude era he rose to Minister of Works, was advanced to Duke of Ying, and also served as area commander of Li and Jing prefectures.

sentences.zh: 貞觀九年卒官，贈禮部尚書，謚曰定。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Zhenguan he died in office; he was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites, with the posthumous name Ding.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenguan 9 he died in office and was posthumously made Minister of Rites, with the posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，以後父累贈司徒，改封周國公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing, as empress's father he was posthumously advanced in succession to Grand Tutor and his enfeoffment was changed to Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Xianqing 1, as the empress's father, he was posthumously advanced to Grand Tutor and re-enfeoffed Duke of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 咸亨中，又贈太尉、太原王，特詔配饗高祖廟庭，列在功臣之上。

translations.literal: In the Xianheng era he was again posthumously appointed Grand Commandant and King of Taiyuan; a special edict ordered him sacrificial companionship in Gaozu's temple hall, ranked above the meritorious ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xianheng era he was again posthumously made Grand Commandant and King of Taiyuan. A special edict ordered him honored with sacrificial companionship in Gaozu's temple hall, ranked above the meritorious ministers.

sentences.zh: 孫承嗣，事在《外戚傳》。

translations.literal: His grandson Chengsi is treated in the "Biographies of External Relatives."
translations.idiomatic: His grandson Chengsi is treated in the Biographies of External Relatives.

sentences.zh: 武士棱鸊長兄士棱，性恭順，勤於稼穡。

translations.literal: Wu Shiling. Shiyi's elder brother Shiling was by nature respectful and compliant and diligent in farming.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shiling. Shiyi's elder brother Shiling was respectful and compliant by nature and diligent in farming.

sentences.zh: 從起義，官至司農少卿，封宣城縣公。

translations.literal: He followed the uprising, rose to Vice Minister of the Directorate of Agriculture, and was enfeoffed Duke of Xuancheng County.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the uprising, rose to Vice Minister of the Directorate of Agriculture, and was enfeoffed Duke of Xuancheng County.

sentences.zh: 常居苑中，委以農囿之事。

translations.literal: He constantly resided in the park precincts and was entrusted with matters of farms and gardens.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in the palace park precincts and was entrusted with farms and gardens.

sentences.zh: 貞觀中卒，贈潭州都督。

translations.literal: He died in the Zhenguan era and was posthumously appointed Area Commander of Tan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the Zhenguan era and was posthumously made Area Commander of Tan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 武士逸次兄士逸，亦有戰功，武德初，為齊王府戶曹，賜爵安陸縣公。

translations.literal: Wu Shiyi—the second elder brother Shiyi. Shiyi also had battle merit; at the beginning of Wude he served as Household Section chief in the Prince of Qi's mansion and was granted the title Duke of Anlu County.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shiyi—the second elder brother Shiyi. He too had battle merit. At the beginning of Wude he served as household section chief in the Prince of Qi's mansion and was granted the title Duke of Anlu County.

sentences.zh: 從齊王鎮并州，為劉武周所獲，於賊中密令人詣京師，陳武周可圖之計。

translations.literal: Following the Prince of Qi in garrisoning Bing Prefecture, he was captured by Liu Wuzhou; while among the enemy he secretly sent someone to the capital to present a plan for how Wuzhou could be overthrown.
translations.idiomatic: Following the Prince of Qi to garrison Bing Prefecture, he was captured by Liu Wuzhou. While held by the enemy he secretly sent a messenger to the capital with a plan to overthrow Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 及武周平，甚見慰勉，累授益州行台左丞。

translations.literal: When Wuzhou was pacified, he was greatly commended and comforted, and was repeatedly appointed Left Assistant of the Yizhou Executive Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: When Wuzhou was pacified he was warmly commended and repeatedly appointed Left Assistant of the Yizhou Executive Headquarters.

sentences.zh: 數陳時政得失，高祖每嘉納之。

translations.literal: He repeatedly set forth the gains and losses of current government policy, and Gaozu always praised and accepted his counsel.
translations.idiomatic: He often presented his views on the strengths and failings of current policy, and Gaozu regularly welcomed and adopted his advice.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，為韶州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: In the early Zhenguan period he was made Prefect of Shao and died.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he became prefect of Shao and died in office.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：唐儉委質義旗之下，立功草昧之初，被拘虜庭，脫高祖蒲州之急；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Tang Jian submitted himself beneath the banner of righteousness, achieved merit in the first days of founding, was detained in the enemy court, and relieved Gaozu's crisis at Pu;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Tang Jian pledged himself under the banner of the righteous army and won merit in the empire's first founding days. Though held captive among the enemy, he averted Gaozu's crisis at Pu;

sentences.zh: 侍獵苑囿，諫太宗馬上之言，可謂純臣矣。

translations.literal: attending the hunt in the park and admonishing Taizong's words on horseback—he may be called a pure minister.
translations.idiomatic: at the hunt in the imperial park he admonished Taizong against ruling from horseback—truly a minister of integrity.

sentences.zh: 順德佐命立功，理郡著明肅之政；

translations.literal: Shunde aided the mandate and achieved merit, and in governing a commandery displayed a clear and stern administration;
translations.idiomatic: Shunde aided the founding mandate and won distinction; as a prefect he earned renown for a clear and stern administration;

sentences.zh: 弘基臨難不屈，陷陣多克捷之勳。

translations.literal: Hongji under hardship did not bend, and in breaking enemy lines won many achievements of swift victory.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji stood unbroken under adversity and, charging the enemy lines, won repeated victories.

sentences.zh: 殷嶠、劉政會、柴嗣昌並在太原，首預舉義，從微至著，善始令終。

translations.literal: Yin Qiao, Liu Zhenghui and Chai Sichang were all at Taiyuan, first among those who joined the uprising, from obscurity to eminence, with a good beginning and a fine end.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Qiao, Liu Zhenghui, and Chai Sichang were all at Taiyuan among the first to join the uprising, rising from obscurity to eminence with honorable beginnings and endings alike.

sentences.zh: 馬三寶出廝養之徒，處將軍之位，亦馬之善走者也。

translations.literal: Ma Sanbao came from the class of stable boys, yet held a general's post—he too was a horse that runs well.
translations.idiomatic: Ma Sanbao rose from stable service to a general's rank—a horse, as it were, that knew how to run.

sentences.zh: 武士鸊首參起義，例封功臣，無戡難之勞，有因人之跡，載窺他傳，過為褒詞。

translations.literal: Wu Shiyi was first among those who joined the uprising and was enfeoffed by precedent as a meritocrat, yet had no labor in quelling hardship and bore traces of riding others' efforts; reading other biographies, the praise is excessive.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Shiyi was among the first to join the uprising and was enfeoffed as a founding meritocrat, yet he did no real work in the struggle and plainly rode others' efforts; other biographies show the praise lavished on him to be excessive.

sentences.zh: 慮當武後之朝，佞出敬宗之筆，凡涉虛美，削而不書。

translations.literal: Fearing that in the era of Empress Wu, flattery issued from Xu Jingzong's brush, whatever involved empty praise has been cut and not written.
translations.idiomatic: Lest the flattery of Xu Jingzong's brush in the era of Empress Wu pass for history, whatever praise proved hollow has been struck from the record.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：茂約忠純，順德功勳。

translations.literal: The encomium says: Maoyue was loyal and pure; Shunde's merit and achievement.
translations.idiomatic: Encomium: Maoyue, loyal and pure; Shunde, merit and achievement.

sentences.zh: 弘基六士，義合風云。

translations.literal: Hongji and the six scholars—righteousness joined with wind and cloud.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji and the founding company—righteous purpose joined with the storm.
